key_insight: SelfCal-QSQN enforces coupled linear constraints through adaptive longitudinal fields, avoiding dense penalty couplers and enabling full-chip constrained quantum annealing.
engineering_relevance: The approach could expand usable problem sizes on sparse quantum annealers for constrained optimization in finance, power grids, and logistics.
method: Encode linear constraints in longitudinal fields using a closed-loop primal-dual scheme.
Estimate dual curvature from single-shot spin-fluctuation covariances.
Apply self-calibrating quasi-Newton updates without penalty couplers, slack qubits, or perturbation queries.
evidence_signal: Across 891 runs on D-Wave Advantage and Advantage2, the study reports 83.3% full-chip exact feasibility, 6.1–20.1× lower high-constraint error than K-scaled first-order updates, and better performance than time-matched mixed-integer programming at 256 spins.
watch_item: Exact feasibility is not guaranteed, and the abstract does not establish broad end-to-end advantage over classical solvers beyond the reported benchmarks.
paper_title: Full-chip constrained quantum annealing via self-calibrating spin-susceptibility control
